# google-oauth-cli

> Command-line tool that creates, rotates, publishes and inspects Google OAuth 2.0
> credentials by automating the Google Cloud Console with Playwright. No API exists for the
> OAuth consent screen, so this drives the web UI instead.

## What it is

`google-oauth-cli` (binary names: `google-oauth-cli`, `gauth`) is a Node.js CLI that automates
the Google Cloud Console's **Google Auth Platform** screens — OAuth clients, client secrets, the
consent screen branding form, the test-user allowlist, and app publishing.

It exists because Google exposes **no API and no `gcloud` command** for the OAuth consent screen.
`gcloud` can create a project and enable APIs, but the client secret, branding, test users and the
publish button are only reachable through the console UI.

## When to use it

- Setting up Google Sign-In (Auth.js / NextAuth, Passport, plain OAuth) for a new project.
- Rotating a leaked or lost `clientSecret` without clicking through the console.
- Debugging "Google login does not work" when the app logs show nothing at all.
- Publishing an app out of Google's **Testing** state to remove the 100-user cap.
- Adding test users to a consent screen that was left with zero (which silently blocks all logins).

## Install

```bash
npm install -g google-oauth-cli
# or
npx google-oauth-cli --help
```

Requirements: Node.js 18+, Google Chrome (or Edge/Chromium), and a Google account with Editor or
Owner access to the GCP project.

## Commands

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `create` | Create an OAuth Web Client (client ID + secret) |
| `renew` | Add a new secret to an existing client |
| `diagnose` | Report publish state, branding gaps, test users, and a fix per blocker |
| `status` | Publish state only |
| `branding` | Read or fill the branding page (home page, privacy policy, terms, developer contact) |
| `publish` | Publish the app to leave the 100-user testing cap |
| `test-users list\|add\|remove` | Manage the test-user allowlist |
| `open [screen]` | Open a console screen in the automated Chrome |
| `kill` | Kill the automation Chrome if it hangs |

All commands accept `--project <id>` and `--json`. Output is a single JSON object on stdout;
progress goes to stderr; exit code is non-zero on failure.

## Key facts an agent must know

1. **A consent screen in Testing with zero test users rejects every login, before the request
   reaches the application.** The app logs stay empty. This is the single most common cause of a
   "broken" Google login. Fix with `gauth test-users add --emails a@x.com,b@y.com`.
2. **Publishing requires a complete branding page**, including publicly reachable privacy policy
   and terms of service URLs. If those pages do not exist, the `publish` button stays disabled and
   saving the branding form silently does not persist.
3. **Testing mode has a hard cap of 100 users over the entire lifetime of the app**, not per year.
4. **`renew` does not invalidate the old secret.** The previous secret keeps working until it is
   deleted in the console, so rotation can be done without downtime.
5. **A gcloud project is required first.** If the project does not exist:
   `gcloud projects create <id> && gcloud config set project <id>`.
6. **The Chrome profile holds a live Google session.** Never commit it. It is gitignored.
7. **Endpoints used**, if you need to build something adjacent:
   - Console screens: `https://console.cloud.google.com/auth/{overview,branding,audience,clients,data-access}?project=<id>`
   - Google OAuth discovery: `https://accounts.google.com/.well-known/openid-configuration`
   - Auth.js v5 callback: `https://<domain>/api/auth/callback/google`
8. **Environment variable names** that consumers typically need:
   - Auth.js v5 / NextAuth: `AUTH_GOOGLE_ID`, `AUTH_GOOGLE_SECRET`
   - Generic: `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`

## Environment variables

`GOOGLE_OAUTH_PROJECT`, `GOOGLE_OAUTH_PROFILE`, `GOOGLE_OAUTH_HOME`, `GOOGLE_OAUTH_PORT`,
`BROWSER_PATH`, `DEBUG`.

## Implementation notes

- Drives your installed Chrome over the Chrome DevTools Protocol (`--remote-debugging-port`),
  so `playwright install` is not needed.
- The console is a heavyweight Angular SPA. `networkidle` never fires; the tool uses
  `domcontentloaded` plus a fixed settle time.
- Saving is triggered with a JS click, because a Playwright `getByRole(...).click()` on the
  Material dialog does not always register the save.
- Console form fields have no `aria-label`; they are located by surrounding text.
